description: Verify the Operation Code field of DUT's emitted ARP Request equals OPERATION_REQUEST (1) — distinguishes a Request from a Reply on the wire (RFC 826 packet generation)
approach:
[Objective]
A single byte distinguishes the two ARP message kinds: opcode 1 is Request, 2 is Reply. When DUT initiates resolution the emitted message must be a Request, not a Reply. This case provokes a DUT ARP Request and asserts the opcode.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. (No cache seeding — DUT's cache for HOST-1-IP starts empty.)

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup message
   ⇒ DUT unicast-Nacks back; cache miss forces an ARP resolution.

3. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → broadcast: ARP Request
      - opcode == 1 (OPERATION_REQUEST)   ← key check
      - sender_mac == DUT iface MAC
      - target_ip  == HOST-1-IP

[Pass condition]
A DUT ARP message whose sender_mac matches the iface is observed and its opcode equals 1.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_opcode — DUT emitted an ARP message but its opcode was not 1 (e.g. unsolicited Reply)
• Fail_timeout — No DUT ARP message observed within the window

verdicts.Fail_opcode: DUT emitted an ARP message with opcode != 1 — not a Request
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No DUT ARP message observed within the window
